topic: DP-3T: The Privacy-First Way to Trace Contact
target_audience: University students in Computer Science or interested tech enthusiasts

sections.title: The Privacy Dilemma
lecture_lines: Digital contact tracing helps stop viral spread quickly.
Centralized systems track everyone on a single server.
DP-3T uses decentralization to protect individual privacy.
animations: Show a network of nodes (people) with a red #FF0000 virus spreading between them.
All nodes connect to a single central server #FFFFFF icon.
Remove the server; show nodes communicating directly with signal waves.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Key Factory (Hash Chains)
lecture_lines: Privacy begins with a secure key hierarchy.
A secret seed generates a unique daily key.
This daily key produces many rotating identifiers.
animations: Display a box labeled 'Secret Key (SK)' in #FFD700 using [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/key.svg].
Draw an arrow from SK to 'Daily Key (DK)' #00FF00 via a hash symbol.
Multiple arrows branch from DK to many small 'RPI' #00BFFF circles.

sections.title: Phase 1: The Secret Handshake (Broadcasting)
lecture_lines: Phones broadcast rotating identifiers every few minutes.
Nearby devices listen and store these random codes.
No identity or location is ever shared.
Codes change frequently to prevent long-term tracking.
animations: A phone icon 'Bolt' emits waves containing code 'RPI-1'.
Phone 'Ace' receives the wave and adds 'RPI-1' to a list.
Show 'Location' and 'ID' labels with a red #FF0000 cross.
Bolt's phone waves cycle through 'RPI-2', 'RPI-3', and 'RPI-4'.

sections.title: Phase 2: The Diagnosis & Upload
lecture_lines: If diagnosed, a user shares their daily keys.
Only keys are uploaded, never location or contacts.
This data is posted to a public board.
The server remains blind to who met whom.
animations: Bolt's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] turns red; an arrow sends 'Daily Key' icon up.
Visual strike-through over map and contact list icons on Bolt's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg].
The 'Daily Key' icon lands on a large 'Public Board' #A9A9A9.
The board shows keys without any lines linking them to users.

sections.title: Phase 3: The Local Match (Verification)
lecture_lines: Phones download daily keys of diagnosed users.
Your phone locally reconstructs all possible identifiers.
It checks these against your stored contact diary.
A match triggers a private exposure notification.
animations: Ace's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] downloads the 'Daily Key' from the public board.
Ace's phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] generates a list of RPIs from the downloaded key.
The generated list is compared against Ace's local 'Diary' [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/diary.svg] list.
A matching entry turns red #FF0000; the phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] flashes a warning.

sections.title: Conclusion: Security & Privacy Recap
lecture_lines: DP-3T ensures identity and location remain private.
Matching happens on your device, not a server.
Technology protecting health and privacy simultaneously.
animations: Show 'Identity' and 'Location' labels with green #00FF00 checkmarks.
Visual of a phone [Asset: /mmfs1/data/group/pmc082/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/phone.svg] processing data next to a blank server.
A heart icon #FF69B4 and a shield icon #4682B4 merge together.
